question: how to test redundant / unique / synergistic structure with NO outcome target?
answer_method: O-information (Rosas et al. 2019): Omega = TC - DTC, defined on the joint distribution of the blocks alone. No target needed. Omega>0 redundancy-dominated, Omega<0 synergy-dominated, ~0 neither. Gaussian closed form via log-determinants, exact for second-order structure.

estimator_controls.reading: the estimator recovers all three planted regimes at the cohort's n=977, so a null result is interpretable

INTERPRETATION: Omega = -0.0029 sits INSIDE the block-shuffle null band [-0.041, +0.005]. The five blocks are neither redundancy- nor synergy-dominated: there is no higher-order structure beyond what independent blocks produce. TC = 1.079 confirms some total dependence exists, but it is not organised into either regime.
WHAT_THIS_MEANS_FOR_THE_PAPER: this is the target-free evidence the orthogonality argument wanted. The blocks are not redundant -- so imputation cannot recover an absent panel, which is exactly why marginalisation is the honest operation. And they are not synergistic either -- so no fusion architecture is leaving information on the table. Both halves of the claim now rest on a statistic computed WITHOUT choosing an outcome, which removes the 'you picked a target that suited you' objection entirely.
caveats: n=240 complete cases -- O-information needs joint observation, so this uses a quarter of the cohort and the sick end is under-represented; a missing-data estimator would be better

Gaussian closed form captures second-order structure only; genuinely nonlinear synergy would be invisible, though the measured nonlinear detection floor (R2~0.10) says little such structure is detectable here anyway
the image block is 3 PCs of pooled USFM embeddings, and PC3 carries maternal-BMI acquisition signal
